item.title: Kumamoto Prefectural Museum — Guide
item.description: The Kumamoto Prefectural Museum, near Suizenji Garden, is a broad, family-friendly museum covering the natural history, geology, archaeology and history of Kumamoto prefecture. Its exhibits range across the region’s dynamic natural environment — shaped by the great Aso volcano — its wildlife and fossils, and its human history from ancient times through the samurai era, presented in an accessible, engaging way. A popular highlight is its planetarium, projecting the night sky and astronomy shows, and there are hands-on and interactive displays that make it especially good for children.

item.title: Lafcadio Hearn Museum & Residence: Old Japan Through Foreign Eyes — Guide
item.description: Lafcadio Hearn, known in Japan as Koizumi Yakumo, was a writer of Greek-Irish background who came to Matsue in 1890, married into a samurai family, took Japanese citizenship, and did more than almost anyone to introduce the culture and folk tales of old Japan to Western readers. His collections of Japanese ghost stories, especially Kwaidan, remain widely read. Beside the castle moat stand two linked sites: the small samurai residence he rented, preserved with the garden he lovingly described, and a modern memorial museum next door displaying his manuscripts, belongings and the story of his life between two worlds.

item.title: Minami Aso Museum & Volcano Science — Guide
item.description: In Minami-Aso (‘southern Aso’), on the floor of the great caldera, this museum introduces the geology, volcanoes, nature and water of the Aso region through accessible exhibits. Aso’s landscape is the product of colossal ancient eruptions and ongoing volcanic activity, and the museum helps visitors understand how the vast caldera formed, how the still-active Nakadake volcano behaves, and how the region’s ecosystems and famous pure spring water are shaped by this volcanic land.

item.title: Miyazaki Prefectural Museum — Guide
item.description: The Miyazaki Prefectural Museum of Nature and History, set in the green surroundings of Miyazaki Jingu shrine’s park in the city, is an excellent free introduction to the prefecture. Its wide-ranging exhibits cover Miyazaki’s natural environment — from its subtropical coast to its mountains and wildlife — as well as its rich archaeology and history, including material connected to the ancient burial mounds of Saitobaru and the region’s deep mythological heritage.

item.title: Nagasaki Museum of History and Culture — Guide
item.description: The Nagasaki Museum of History and Culture, in the Tateyama district, is devoted to the city’s remarkable history as Japan’s principal gateway for overseas trade and cultural exchange during its centuries of isolation. Its well-designed exhibits explore how goods, people, religions and ideas from China, the Netherlands and beyond flowed through Nagasaki, shaping a uniquely cosmopolitan local culture — from imported art and crafts to the fusion food and festivals still seen today.

item.title: Saga Prefectural Museum and Art Museum — Guide
item.description: The Saga Prefectural Museum and the adjoining Saga Prefectural Art Museum, set together beside the greenery of Saga Castle park in the heart of the city, form the prefecture’s main cultural complex. The museum covers Saga’s natural history, archaeology and history — including material connected to the Yoshinogari ancient site, the prefecture’s important role in Japan’s modernisation, and its ceramics and culture — through well-presented exhibits. The art museum next door displays works by artists connected to Saga alongside changing exhibitions.

item.title: Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial Museum, Kochi — Guide
item.description: Sakamoto Ryoma is Kochi’s greatest hero: a low-ranking samurai from Tosa who became a visionary of the movement to overthrow the shogunate, broker alliances and open Japan to the modern world, only to be assassinated in Kyoto at just 31. This striking modern museum, perched on the headland above Katsurahama beach where his famous statue stands, tells his life and turbulent times through letters, artefacts and immersive displays, with dramatic ocean views from its galleries.

item.title: Siebold Memorial Museum — Guide
item.description: The Siebold Memorial Museum, in the Narutaki district where the physician once lived, honours Philipp Franz von Siebold, the German doctor who arrived at the Dutch trading post of Dejima in 1823 and became one of the most important figures in the exchange of knowledge between Japan and the West. At his private school Narutaki-juku he taught Western medicine and science to Japanese students, while himself studying and cataloguing Japanese plants, animals and culture, sending vast collections back to Europe that shaped Western understanding of Japan.

item.title: Yamaga Lantern Craft & Museum — Guide
item.description: The town of Yamaga in northern Kumamoto is famous for its Yamaga-tōrō, extraordinary paper lanterns and models made using a craft passed down for centuries. Astonishingly, these intricate golden lanterns — from the classic ‘kintōrō’ headdress worn by festival dancers to elaborate miniature shrines, castles and buildings — are constructed entirely from washi (Japanese paper) and glue alone, with no wooden or metal frames whatsoever, yet are remarkably strong and precise.

item.title: Hyogo's Museum of Nature and Human Activities — Guide
item.description: The Museum of Nature and Human Activities in Sanda is one of the largest natural history museums in western Japan, built around research collections rather than spectacle. Its halls run from minerals and fossils through the ecology of the Seto Inland Sea to the human shaping of the Hyogo landscape, and its most celebrated subject is close to home: the discovery of the sauropod dinosaur Tambatitanis in the Tamba hills, whose excavation and reconstruction the museum has led.

item.title: Nara National Museum: Masterpieces of Buddhist Art — Guide
item.description: The Nara National Museum, set within Nara Park, is Japan’s premier museum of Buddhist art, its elegant Meiji-era Main Building and modern galleries housing a superb permanent collection of Buddhist statues, paintings, sutras and ritual objects spanning centuries. Its most famous event is the annual Shosoin Exhibition each autumn, when a rotating selection of the fabled 8th-century treasures of the Shosoin — the imperial repository at Todaiji, holding artifacts from along the Silk Road — goes on rare public display, drawing visitors from across the country.

item.title: Hamamatsu: Japan's City of Musical Instruments — Guide
item.description: Hamamatsu is Japan’s city of music, the birthplace and home of Yamaha, Kawai and Roland, whose factories grew from the city’s craft traditions into the instruments played on stages worldwide. The centrepiece for visitors is the Hamamatsu Museum of Musical Instruments, the only public museum of its kind in Japan, displaying some 1,500 instruments from every corner of the world with headphone stations to hear them and a hands-on room where many can actually be played, while piano fans can also tour associated factory and brand facilities.

item.title: Ibaraki Prefectural Museum of History: From Ancient Times to the Mito Domain — Guide
item.description: The Ibaraki Prefectural Museum of History offers a comprehensive overview of the prefecture’s past, from archaeological artefacts of ancient settlement through the feudal era of the powerful Mito Tokugawa domain, one of three branch families of the ruling shogunate. Exhibits cover local archaeology, folk traditions, and the intellectual and political legacy of Mito scholarship, which played an influential role in the ideas leading up to the Meiji Restoration. The museum grounds include a pleasant garden and a relocated historic building, set within walking distance of Mito Castle Remains.

item.title: Aomori Museum of Art: Yoshitomo Nara's Aomori Dog — Guide
item.description: The Aomori Museum of Art is home to Yoshitomo Nara’s colossal 8.5-metre ‘Aomori Dog’, the white puppy that has become the prefecture’s modern icon. Jun Aoki’s half-buried white architecture echoes the archaeological trenches of the neighbouring Jomon site. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Aomori City, Aomori Hours ~9:30–17:00 (closed some Mon) Admission Around ¥510 (more for shows) Time needed 1–1.

item.title: Nebuta Museum WA RASSE: Aomori's Festival Year-Round — Guide
item.description: Right beside Aomori Station, the Nebuta Museum WA RASSE lets you experience Aomori’s greatest festival any day of the year. Five of the towering illuminated warrior floats from recent Nebuta Festivals are displayed indoors, close enough to see every brushstroke and wire. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Aomori City (by Aomori Station) Hours 9:00–18:00 (seasonal) Admission Around ¥620 Time needed About 1–1.

item.title: Upopoy Ainu Museum Guide: Tickets, Highlights & Access
item.description: Upopoy (the National Ainu Museum and Park) at Shiraoi is Japan’s flagship centre for the culture of the Ainu, the Indigenous people of Hokkaido and the north. Opened in 2020 on the shore of Lake Poroto, this thoughtful complex tells the Ainu story — their language, beliefs, crafts and connection to nature — long marginalised and now celebrated. With a modern museum, traditional houses, live music and dance, craft demonstrations and hands-on workshops, Upopoy is a moving, eye-opening stop that adds real depth to a Hokkaido trip.

item.title: Kurashiki Bikan Quarter: Canal District, Ohara Museum, and Craft Shopping
item.description: Kurashiki sits 16 minutes west of Okayama by train, but in character it belongs to a different world. Where Okayama City is a modern prefectural capital with castle gardens and department stores, Kurashiki preserves a dense quarter of Edo-period architecture that survived the 20th century largely intact. The Bikan Historic Quarter — a cluster of white-walled earthen storehouses (kura) along a narrow canal lined with willows — is among the best-preserved merchant districts in Japan, and one of the few that has found a productive second life as a center for arts and crafts rather than simply as a museum piece.
